title: Handoff auto-clear mod

domains.title: How does a finished handoff turn into a cleared, resumed session?
checks: Every skip path leaves the printed pointer usable.
The pointer is submitted exactly once per clear.

decisions.title: How does the mod learn a handoff just finished?

options.label: Flag file written by the skill
options.why: Explicit signal; a quoted pointer cannot trigger a clear. Costs one extra skill step.

options.label: Scan the final reply for the pointer
options.why: No skill change, but a pasted or discussed pointer could clear the session unattended.

options.label: tmux send-keys watcher
options.why: Works without mods but needs tmux, idle detection and pane discovery.

decisions.whyPick: User chose A: explicit signal, no false clears.

slots.scale: One small file per handoff under ~/.claude/handoff/; stale ones are deleted after 30 minutes.
slots.dataFrom: Written by the handoff skill from the collector's session id and the pointer line.

more.why: A wrong clear unattended costs the live context.

decisions.title: Is auto-clear opt-in or always on?

options.label: Always after /handoff
options.why: Unattended continuation is the point; no extra argument to remember.

options.label: Opt-in per invocation
options.why: Safer, but the session sits idle whenever the user forgets.

decisions.whyPick: User: always clear automatically; the goal is not to wait at the computer.

slots.scale: Every handoff clears; the guards in D3 bound a runaway chain.
slots.dataFrom: No input; behaviour is fixed, only the guard gap is configurable.

more.why: Unattended resume only helps if it needs no per-run choice.

decisions.title: What stops a runaway handoff loop?

options.label: 3 clears per hour
options.why: Simple but blocks a genuinely intensive session.

options.label: Minimum 10 min since last auto-clear, 12 per hour backstop
options.why: A loop is a run of short cycles; healthy sessions live 20+ minutes. Gap is a plugin option, 0 disables.

decisions.whyPick: User agreed 3/hour is too stringent for heavy sessions; age-based guard fits.

slots.scale: When refused, the mod toasts the reason and the printed pointer is the manual fallback. Two sessions in one project share the guard on purpose: a loop in either is a loop.
slots.dataFrom: Last-clear timestamps in $.store keyed per project directory (the store file is shared by all sessions); gap from userConfig minGapMinutes.

more.why: The depth-8 'is Done met' check in the note is model-side only.

decisions.title: Where do the mod files live next to the existing command hooks?

options.label: Add a modules entry to the existing hooks/hooks.json
options.why: One manifest, nothing new to install. Needs claude plugin validate to accept hooks and modules together.

options.label: Second hooks file named in plugin.json
options.why: Keeps the two shapes apart, but depends on plugin.json supporting a second hooks path.

options.label: Separate plugin session-autoclear
options.why: Always valid and optional to install, but a second install and a skill that depends on a sibling plugin.

slots.scale: Affects install only; no runtime cost.
slots.dataFrom: claude plugin validate output on a scratch copy decides which of a/b is legal.

more.why: The command-hook file has shape {hooks:{...}} and the mod file {modules:[...]}.

decisions.whyPick: One manifest, nothing new to install. Needs claude plugin validate to accept hooks and modules together.

decisions.title: How does the pointer reach the new session after the clear?

options.label: Hold it in the mod instance, submit from session.start after the clear
options.why: Each Claude Code process has its own instance, so two sessions cannot collide. The instance survives /clear (auto-clear-context relies on this). Lost only if the process dies mid-clear.

options.label: Park it in the shared store
options.why: Survives a restart, but session.start carries no id of the previous session, so concurrent clears in one project cannot tell whose pointer is whose.

options.label: Await the clear, then submit in the same hook
options.why: Fewest parts, but depends on the hook surviving the clear.

slots.scale: One variable per instance, cleared after submit; a crash between clear and submit loses it and the printed pointer is the fallback.
slots.dataFrom: Pointer read from the flag file before the clear and held in the instance.

more.why: session.start has no previous-session id and no source field in 2.1.332, so the new session cannot look anything up by the old id.

decisions.whyPick: Each Claude Code process has its own instance, so two sessions cannot collide. The instance survives /clear (auto-clear-context relies on this). Lost only if the process dies mid-clear.

decisions.title: Who writes the flag file?

options.label: New script arm_autoclear.py called from skill step 5
options.why: Deterministic and unit-testable like collect.py; the model cannot get the format wrong.

options.label: SKILL.md tells the model to Write the file
options.why: No new script, but format and path depend on the model each time.

slots.scale: Tiny script, runs once per handoff.
slots.dataFrom: Arguments: session id and pointer line, both already known from the collector.

more.why: Same reason the collector names the note path instead of the model.

decisions.whyPick: Deterministic and unit-testable like collect.py; the model cannot get the format wrong.

decisions.title: When a check fails, drop the flag or retry later?

options.label: Drop the flag, toast the reason, user clears by hand
options.why: Simple; a draft or interrupt means the user is back, so they drive.

options.label: Keep the flag and retry at the next turn.complete until it expires
options.why: More automatic, but it can clear a session the user has since resumed working in.

slots.scale: No timers or retries to leak.
slots.dataFrom: turn.complete reason ('aborted' marks an interrupt) and $.prompt.read() for the draft; both confirmed in the 2.1.332 types.

more.why: An interrupt or draft is the signal that a person is present.

decisions.whyPick: Simple; a draft or interrupt means the user is back, so they drive.

tasks.title: Pure decision function autoclear.ts

interfaces.consumes: Nothing from the engine; plain values only
interfaces.produces: decide(i: {flag: Flag | null; nowSec: number; reason: 'answer'|'aborted'|'refusal'|'error'; draft: string; lastClearSec: number | undefined; clearsLastHour: number; minGapMinutes: number}): {action: 'clear'} | {action: 'skip'; reason: string; dropFlag: boolean; notify: boolean}. Constants FLAG_TTL_SEC = 1800, BACKSTOP_PER_HOUR = 12

steps.title: Write the failing tests
steps.body: Base input: flag {session_id:'s', pointer:'read /n.md — HANDOFF v1 mode=mid parent=s', created_at:1000}, nowSec 1100, reason 'answer', draft '', lastClearSec undefined, clearsLastHour 0, minGapMinutes 10.

code.text:
test('clears when every check passes', () => expect(decide(base)).toEqual({ action: 'clear' }))
test('no flag is a silent skip', () => expect(decide({ ...base, flag: null })).toEqual({ action: 'skip', reason: 'no-flag', dropFlag: false, notify: false }))
test('flag older than 1800 s is dropped', () => expect(decide({ ...base, nowSec: 2801 })).toEqual({ action: 'skip', reason: 'stale-flag', dropFlag: true, notify: true }))
test('flag exactly 1800 s old still fires', () => expect(decide({ ...base, nowSec: 2800 })).toEqual({ action: 'clear' }))
test('aborted turn drops the flag', () => expect(decide({ ...base, reason: 'aborted' })).toEqual({ action: 'skip', reason: 'interrupted', dropFlag: true, notify: true }))
test('a draft drops the flag', () => expect(decide({ ...base, draft: 'abc' })).toEqual({ action: 'skip', reason: 'draft', dropFlag: true, notify: true }))
test('599 s since last clear refuses', () => expect(decide({ ...base, lastClearSec: 501 })).toEqual({ action: 'skip', reason: 'min-gap', dropFlag: true, notify: true }))
test('600 s since last clear passes', () => expect(decide({ ...base, lastClearSec: 500 })).toEqual({ action: 'clear' }))
test('12 clears in the hour refuses', () => expect(decide({ ...base, clearsLastHour: 12 })).toEqual({ action: 'skip', reason: 'backstop', dropFlag: true, notify: true }))
test('minGapMinutes 0 disables the gap but not the backstop', () => { expect(decide({ ...base, lastClearSec: 1099, minGapMinutes: 0 })).toEqual({ action: 'clear' }); expect(decide({ ...base, clearsLastHour: 12, minGapMinutes: 0 }).action).toBe('skip') })

steps.title: Implement decide()
steps.body: Check in this order: no flag, stale (age > FLAG_TTL_SEC), reason !== 'answer', draft !== '', gap (only when minGapMinutes > 0 and lastClearSec defined and nowSec - lastClearSec < minGapMinutes*60), backstop. Export Flag type and both constants.

steps.title: Write the failing tests
steps.body: Using the engine kit: a fresh flag for the current session plus reason 'answer' leads to one /clear; after session.start the pointer is submitted exactly once; with no flag nothing runs; a skip shows a toast and deletes the flag; a second arm inside 10 minutes is refused.

code.text:
test('fresh flag clears once and submits the pointer once', async () => { /* seed flag file, raise turn.complete, assert one command.run {command:'clear'}, raise session.start, assert one prompt.submit with the flag pointer */ })
test('no flag does nothing', async () => { /* raise turn.complete, assert no command.run and no toast */ })
test('draft skips, toasts the reason and deletes the flag', async () => { /* prompt.read returns draft 'x' */ })

steps.title: Implement register()
steps.body: On turn.complete: read <session-id>.autoclear (ignore other sessions' flags), read the draft with $.prompt.read(), the per-project clear history from $.store, call decide(). On clear: hold the pointer in a module variable, record the timestamp, delete the flag, run $.command.run({command:'clear'}). On session.start: if a held pointer exists, submit it once and drop it. On a skip with notify: $.ui.toast('auto-clear skipped: <reason>') and delete the flag when dropFlag.

steps.title: Register the module and option
steps.body: Add the modules entry to hooks/hooks.json (as validated in T1), add userConfig minGapMinutes to plugin.json, bump the version, add a README line on what the mod does and that mods must be allowed.

scenarios.title: Handoff clears and resumes
scenarios.expected: After the handoff turn the session runs /clear and the pointer is submitted once in the new session.

scenarios.title: Ordinary answer
scenarios.expected: No flag means no clear, no toast, no cost.

scenarios.title: Stale flag
scenarios.expected: A flag older than 30 minutes is deleted and never fires.

scenarios.title: Draft or interrupt
scenarios.expected: The flag is dropped, a toast says why, the printed pointer still works.

scenarios.title: Second handoff within 10 minutes
scenarios.expected: The clear is refused with a toast; the manual pointer remains.

scenarios.title: Two sessions at once
scenarios.expected: Each session clears and resumes its own pointer; the age guard is per project.

scenarios.title: No mod support
scenarios.expected: Behaviour is today's: pointer printed, user clears by hand.

goal: After /session:handoff writes its note, the session clears itself and the successor starts from the pointer with nobody at the keyboard.
architecture: A hooks module (mod) in the session plugin listens for turn.complete. The handoff skill arms it with a per-session flag file holding the pointer; the mod runs /clear, then submits the pointer in the new session, behind a minimum-age guard.
techStack: Claude Code 2.1.332 mod API (TypeScript hooks module, $.command.run, $.prompt.submit, $.store), Python 3 for the skill-side script and tests, claude plugin test for the mod.
summary: The handoff skill drops a flag file; the mod sees it at turn end.
The mod clears the session, then submits the pointer so work continues unattended.
A minimum age between auto-clears stops a runaway handoff loop.
constraints: Without mod support the skill behaves exactly as today: the pointer is always printed.
The submitted pointer keeps the HANDOFF v1 sentinel so record-session-metrics.js still links parent and child.
No auto-clear fires mid-turn, after a user interrupt, over a draft, or from a flag older than 30 minutes.
Existing SessionStart:clear hooks (pivot-gate, inherit-handoff-title) must still fire on the auto clear.
The age guard is keyed per project; the pointer lives in the mod instance, never in the shared store.

reviewFocus.text: Flag exactly 1800 s old fires; 1801 s is dropped.
Turn interrupted (reason aborted) with a fresh flag: no clear, flag dropped.
Pointer submitted exactly once, and only in the session after the clear.
Two sessions writing the shared store at once do not corrupt it.
